sources.evidence: Legacy clip-space diagonal/offset and fixed [0,1] host depth. TransformVertices copies all four payload DWORDs, reports raw logical homogeneous coordinates, offscreen is the intersection of clip flags. Rejected output values and unsafe pointers/undersized strides are not pinned native contracts.
TRANSFORM uses D3DFVF_LVERTEX and TRANSFORMLIGHT uses D3DFVF_VERTEX. Wine marks NOCOLOR and UPDATEEXTENTS incomplete; bounded project behavior is tested separately.
Legacy Set/Get projection cache and input * oldLogicalProjection Multiply order; physical logicalProjection * clipspace.
Windows position/payload, scale, clipping, offscreen and D3DVIEWPORT2 vectors around 12500-13130.
Wine multiply_matrix uses reversed parameter order, unlike project d3d7_multiply_matrix.

reference.scope: S2-52: execute TRANSFORM retains LVERTEX diffuse/specular/UV and does not require lighting preparation. Legacy V1 scale and V2 clip rectangle/depth are composed after logical application projection; host viewport depth is always [0,1]. Device2/3 logical Set/Get/Multiply, Execute STATETRANSFORM, GPU draws, CPU ProcessVertices and explicit-viewport TransformVertices share effective projection. TransformVertices preserves 16-byte payload, raw pre-clip homogeneous output and exact offscreen clip intersection; explicit noncurrent viewport does not mutate current state. Existing bounded stride/NULL validation and zero-W policy are retained rather than reproducing native crashes; undersized output/input strides are refused. Rejected XYZW is Wine implementation behavior, not a native test oracle. NOCOLOR retains both stored colors and UPDATEEXTENTS/source bounds are project regression contracts, not full native conformance claims. Native 2281 checks, 128 reactivations and 128 prelit passes, 16 runtime mutants, ASAN/UBSAN and old actual viewport/execute functions with new helper definitions runtime control. XP 2 viewports x3 projections x3 draw routes =18 readbacks, 36 CPU position/payload checks and 12 logical projection queries. CPU replies are explicit transport controls, not GPU pixel evidence. Actual SwiftShader and Metal replay checks independent 16x16 color/coverage/depth scene expectations with explicit LIGHTING=FALSE for the prelit scene; Clear touches the viewport only and the rest of the initially zero texture remains zero. Mixed Device7/legacy state-block private metadata, full viewport validation quirks, execute clipping/lighting flag conformance, S2-53/54/55/57, broad ownership/Reset/thread/device-loss/format, native HAL, games/FPS and review stages4/5/6 remain open. Host/protocol/shader/bundle and D3D8/9 unchanged.

xp.rendering: Actual D3D1 execute TRANSFORM and D3D2/3 LVERTEX draws; two legacy viewports, logical/effective projection separation, ordered Multiply and repeated activation; 36 CPU transformed vertices with full payloads, 18 actual draw/readback requests. XP reply pixels are simulated transport controls; independent dual GPU replay checks rendered colors, coverage, clip and depth mapping

validationRepairs: The first strict build found cache fields inserted into the state-block declaration instead of D3D7Device; this was corrected before any accepted XP capture. Frozen Windows tests also establish four payload DWORDs, so the retained bounded input/output stride guard is 32 bytes and all sixteen payload bytes are copied.

The old actual legacy functions are compiled with new clip/projection helper definitions. The old viewport depth conversion then fails the runtime viewport assertion; this is not presented as an old whole-bundle run.

The first wire reader treated raw D3D2/3 LVERTEX as pretransformed TLVERTEX. It now separately asserts raw XYZ/reserved and execute XYZRHW, exact colors/UVs, index bytes, live viewport and physical projection; production/capture were unchanged for this reader repair.

The first GPU control retained default lighting for raw immediate draws and assumed Clear covered the entire target. The SDK now explicitly requests an unlit prelit scene, and independent expected pixels preserve zero outside the current viewport. The earlier source/capture/GPU artifact is retained under stage4i7-first-lighting-control; production was unchanged, and accepted XP capture is fresh. Full default-lighting/non-normal-FVF behavior is not claimed.

Rejected TransformVertices XYZW follows Wine implementation behavior rather than a native oracle. Crash-prone NULL/stride quirks, full NOCOLOR/UPDATEEXTENTS conformance and mixed Device7/legacy state-block private metadata remain excluded.
